says: In next/, the scenario 'saved waits survive object sleep, object abort and workerd replacement' waits a fixed 12 s of wall clock for workerd's own idle eviction (line 547) and then polls in loops with no end of their own, so it needs 17 to 20 s on a quiet runner and has no margin when the runner is slow.
proof: It timed out at 60 s once, in https://github.com/kamp-us/tea-fabrika/actions/runs/43334569348/job/131588023241 (attempt 1 on the t883-wire-flake branch, `Error: Test timed out in 60000ms.`), and the rerun of that same run went green. In the 20 passing runs of it in the CI logs of 2026-11-12 to 2026-11-14 it took 17.3 to 20.0 s (median 20.0 s). The P2 supervision law timed out in the same job at the same time, which points at that job's machine being slow rather than at one law alone.
cost: On a slow runner this scenario goes red with no bug, now on the 3-hour schedule where it runs as an integration test.
